name: Repentance & assurance
about: Godly sorrow, confession, and the believer kept by God.

teachings.title: Forgiveness is not earned by penance
teachings.summary: Like Esau compounding his trespass to regain favor, we cannot earn forgiveness by penance; God forgives by grace and mercy those who sincerely confess and turn, as the prodigal son did.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 26**
*34* *And Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite:*

*35 Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.*

**Genesis 27**
*46 And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these which are of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me*?

To catch us up, Esau, the oldest and heir by law to the inheritance of Issac, and by the blessing passed from Abraham to Isaac, heir to the promise of God, had sold his birthright to his younger twin, Jacob for a bowl of lentils. Jacob then, many years later, under direction of Rebekah, fooled Issac into also giving him the blessing.

Esau had also taken two wives of the Hittites, a heathen people of Canaan. This had greatly displeased their mother, Rebekah and Isaac.

And so Esau's anger at Jacob, a murderous rage, presented an opportunity; send Jacob away to Rebekah's people, Abraham's cousins, to find a suitable wife and return once Esau had calmed down.

And so, Jacob flees back to Padanaram, *to the house of Bethuel thy mother's father; and take thee a wife from thence of the daughers of Laban thy mother's brother*.

Before leaving, Issac gives Jacob his blessing again, this time without guile or subterfuge.

*God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a multitude of people; And give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee; that thou mayest inherit the land wherein thou art a stranger, which God gave unto Abraham.*

Seeing Issac blessing his brother, that he was sent to the daughters of Laban for a wife and knowing his own wives disappointed his parents, Esau tries to *work* to regain their favor by marrying a daughter of his uncle, Ishmael. Thinking this will help, but like most of our efforts to please people after making mistakes, it only compounds his trespass now having multiple wives.

Poor Esau, now Edom. We find in life, as well as before God, what others want isn't for us to "make it right" so much as to stop digging, and be sincere in asking for forgiveness. Penance isn't how we earn forgiveness. Forgiveness is given by grace and mercy, charitable love extended to a sincere change of heart and contrition, acknowledging what we've done and how it impacted others.

**Isaiah 1:18**
*Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.*

**Isaiah 55:7**
*Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the LORD, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.*

**1 John 1:9**
*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*.

We see this idea of Biblical contrition and forgiveness in the parable of the Prodigal Son, who realizing his sin, turns back to his father, repenting of his decision to waste his inheritance with harlots and wine;

**Luke 15**
*18 I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,*

*19 And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.*

*20 And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.*

*21 And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.*

*22 But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:*

*23 And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:*

*24 For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.*

teachings.title: His mercies are new every morning
teachings.summary: A saved believer still carrying guilt should believe God's irrevocable promise that his sins are blotted out and remembered no more, and that it is never too late to turn back to the Father, whose mercies are new every morning.
teachings.text:
**Lamentations 3:22-23**
*It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.*

**Hebrews 10:16-17**
*This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them; And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.*

**Psalm 103:12**
*As far as the east is from the west, So far hath he removed our transgressions from us.*

**Isaiah 43:25**
*I, even I, am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake, and will not remember thy sins.*

**Romans 11:29**
*For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance.*

Isaiah 38:17
*Behold, for peace I had great bitterness: but thou hast in love to my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption: for thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back.*

If you are a believer, saved by faith in Christ Jesus and have been forgiven for your sins, and you still carry that burden of guilt, if you haven't given it to God to cast behind His back, to remove them from you as far as the east is from the west, to have your inequities blotted out forever, then please consider His word. Believe His promises, for they are without repentance. Irrevocable. He has promised to cleanse you of that burden, to redeem you as His sons.

*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*.

No matter how backslidden. No matter how snared in sin. No matter how the devil accuses you before God, in Christ Jesus you are forgiven.

If you screwed up today, the Bible says that God's mercy is new every morning. We can choose to take up the cross again, to turn towards Him and do His will, every single day. To earnestly strive for the prize. To contend for the faith. To feed the new man and starve the old. To w*alk in the Spirit,* and not *fulfil the lust of the flesh.*

For a saved believer who has been sealed by the Spirit, it is never too late to turn to back to God and away from your sins. Like the Prodigal son, returning to the Father. And like that parable, the Father will rise to meet you, and celebrate your return. And your sin and inequities He will remember no more.

teachings.title: David's repentance versus Cain's sorrow
teachings.summary: Unlike Cain, who only grieved his punishment, David as a saved man grieves his sin itself, and confession and a plea for mercy are the only way out of the Lord's chastening.
teachings.text:
It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the Loving God. The Lord's chastening can be fierce, and our wish should be to acknowledge our wrongdoing, and fear God.

Recognizing the predicaments we may find ourselves in are our own making, and calling upon the Lord to help is the only way out of whatever we have fallen into. Whatever snare we are caught in. Whatever arrows the Lord sends our way as a wake-up call, there is no relief except confession and a plea for mercy from the longsuffering God of our salvation.

In **Genesis 4**, we find Cain being cursed with punishment from the Lord for the first murder, the blood of Cain's brother, righteous Abel, and he says to the Lord;

**Genesis 4:13**
*And Cain said unto the LORD, My punishment is greater than I can bear.*

There was no remorse for what he had done, just sorrow at the consequence. But David paints the picture of a repentant sinner, recognizing that the punishment must be just, because it comes from God.

*There is no soundness in my flesh because of thine anger; neither is there any rest in my bones because of my sin.*

Where Cain went about his day, and lied without a qualm when asked of God about Abel; *Am I my brother's keeper?*

In contrast, David, as a saved believer, has become unable to rest because of the guilt his sin carries. It is his iniquities that are the burden he cannot bear.

Faced with his sin and the consequences, it is David's sin that worries him more.

We should keep this perspective. To not go the way of Cain. Notice too, that rather than seeking healing and relief from the punishment by confession and having a contrite heart, Cain's concern is for his own life. God leaves a mark on Cain to ensure he lives and suffers for it.

But we who are His are commanded to hate iniquity. Even our own. Especially our own.

**Romans 12:9**
*Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.*

**Proverbs 8:13**
*The fear of the LORD is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate*.

David sees the wounds caused by his sin as festering and infected, stinking. Literal or metaphorical, we all see the damage of sin in our lives. The harm it's caused.

We may not be spared the consequences, but we need not continue in the chastening that comes with unconfessed sin.

The loathsome disease that rots our flesh, that makes us feeble and sore broken. The disquietude of our hearts. This may be spiritual, it may be in our soul and how we feel, it may be the effect of sin in our bodies, literal and tangible.

Sin manifests in our hearts and in our bodies, and brings men to conviction when we fear God.

David, who in **Psalm 32** sang of the blessedness of the man whose sins are forgiven, covered and not imputed against them, is now singing of the wounds, failing strength, bitter loneliness as a result of his actions. Abandoned and betrayed.

In his sin, he has made friends with those that seek His life. He was deaf to their intentions. He did not speak up against them. Now he's between the reproof of God and the mischief of the wicked, and has no recourse but to seek the Lord.

*For in thee, O LORD, do I hope: thou wilt hear, O Lord my God.*

No matter how desperate our situation, no matter how foolish or wicked we've been, no matter the cause for our misery; be it the chastening of the Lord or the betrayal of those we've given breadth to do evil, the mercies of our Father, seeking His face and His grace, are always there for those who have trusted in Him. He has promised. God Who cannot lie. Almighty God. So we know we can turn to Him.

Because He is our hope. Because evildoers may magnify themselves in our failures. Because we are willing to admit we are helpless without Him. To come up halt, stumbling and falling, unable to go on. Sorrow continually before us.

Because we declare our iniquity, admitting our wrongdoing, being sorry for what we have done.

For these reasons, we can cry out to the Lord with confidence to deliver us.

teachings.title: David's cry of contrition
teachings.summary: Psalm 51 shows how a believer under God's judgment should come in humble worship and confession, trusting that God is faithful to forgive and cleanse even sins like David's.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 51** is the clearest and most sober cry of contrition and supplication for forgiveness by a believer, in the face of a judgment by the Almighty God, that we have in Scripture.

It is David at his lowest. "A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bath-sheba."

We know the story. David doesn't go off to war as kings were expected to. He stays at his place and sees Bathsheba, the wife of his soldier, Uriah the Hittite, bathing on her nearby roof. Filled with lust, he has her. And as a consequence of that adultery, David conspired to have Uriah killed in battle, and wed his pregnant widow.

Nathan confronts the King, and the Lord curses David for his sin;

**2 Samuel 12:7–10**
*And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul; And I gave thee thy master’s house, and thy master’s wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that had been too little, I would moreover have given unto thee such and such things. Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the LORD, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon. Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.*

The judgment of God was given, the child should die.

**2 Samuel 12:14–15**
*Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die. And Nathan departed unto his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s wife bare unto David, and it was very sick.*

David fasts and prays and stays by the child's side, but in the end the illness takes the boy.

**2 Samuel 12:18–19**
*And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he would not hearken unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead? But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.*

David, devastated, cleans himself and goes into the house of the Lord to worship. It is in this context that this Psalm was written.

Rather than a root of bitterness against the judgement of God, as many are tempted to take on in the face of such fierce judgement, David concedes and comes to the Lord, asking for mercy. As he has so often in **Psalms**, he begins in worship, praising God for His lovingkindness and mercy. Reminding himself, and the Lord of His great qualities, and appeals to the ultimate judge to blot out his transgressions.

This is a formula of prayer that we should commit to our prayer life. Under better circumstances and joyous events, or in grave repentance and regret for whatever sins we have committed, the Lord should be approached in humility and meekness of spirit. Hallowing His holy name.

The request is to forgive the confessed transgressions, knowing He is merciful and faithful to forgive His children.

**1 John 1:9**
*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*.

This same promise applies to believers, today. The sure knowledge that our heavenly Father is faithful to forgive us, even the sins of the level of David. To wash us throughly, to cleanse us. To blot the iniquity from our record, and heal us, and our relationship with God.

But note, it is if we confess our sins. David acknowledged his transgressions. We cannot lie to God and we should not lie to ourselves. We cannot hide from our sin when we've faced judgment, and our conscience keeps the sin ever before us in guilt.

teachings.title: Our flesh sins, not the new man
teachings.summary: Honest confession brings forgiveness through Christ's blood, and sin is not imputed to the believer because it is the flesh that sins, not the new man born of God.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Psalm 51**, having established the context and getting the contention on the false doctrine of original sin guilt that comes from a shallow reading of the text, we see the purpose of the Psalm is the honest confession of a righteous man.

David is not placing the blame of what he has done on anyone else, and accepts full responsibility for whatever God judges against him. His fear of the Lord has led him to Godly repentance and reconciliation.

*Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom*.

This is the meekness and honesty about our sin that God seeks, that in it, we can actually learn from Him and grow.

We discussed in the previous **Psalm 50** study that God doesn't seek the sacrifices and burnt offerings, but a meek and contrite heart. He is pleased as a Father when we come to Him for restitution and forgiveness. His mercy and grace are limitless, all He asks for is honesty in our heart.

*For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.*

David confesses, and calls upon the Lord to purge him with hyssop, the sponge like plant that was used to apply the blood on the posts during the first passover, the same that was present when the Lord was crucified and they gave Him gall to drink.

The washing of forgiveness by the blood of Christ is ours, that we become white as snow.

**Isaiah 1:18**
*Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.*

David pleads to be made to hear joy and gladness, to be cheered by the power of God's word to heal the brokenness he feels from the Father's chastening.

He asks God to hide His face from David's sins. To see them and remember them no more. To blot out his iniquity.

We know as saved Christians that this promise of God, to forgive our sins past, present and future, that He will remember them no more and place them as far from us as east is from west, is our blessed hope in the redemption that is found in Christ.

We take comfort in this truth when we are faithful to confess to Him;

**1 John 1:7–10**
*But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.*

This promise shows not only the faithfulness of God to forgive, but also that our sin in the flesh is not held against our ledger in Heaven. It is not imputed against those that are in Christ.

**1 John 3:9**
*Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God.*

John is not contradicting himself by saying if we say we have no sin, we are liars and simultaneously saying we cannot sin, being born of God.

He is describing the same feelings from the failure of the flesh David writes about here.

When we sin, it is not the new man, created in Christ, but the flesh.

**Romans 7:15–17**
*For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I. If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good. Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.*

Our flesh sins. If we deny that we are liars. But by being born again in Christ, we do not sin. The difference is that the flesh, which we can mortify to sin, and restrain from our lusts, is dead. Nailed to the cross with Christ.

**Galatians 5:24–25**
*And they that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts. If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.*

teachings.title: The man to whom the Lord imputeth not sin
teachings.summary: Repentance from dead works to faith in God saves by faith alone, and God promises not to impute sin to the believer but to remember it no more.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 6:1**
*Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God*

Repentance from dead works and to faith towards God. Turning from means turning towards. From trusting in our works of righteousness to faith in God. This is the foundation that is built on the rock that is Christ.

And so, reckoned of faith, the man who does no works but believes, is saved by that faith alone. Paul quotes Davin from **Psalm 32**
*Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, Whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man unto whom the LORD imputeth not iniquity, And in whose spirit there is no guile*.

The Lord will not impute sin, our ledger is clean, our transgressions forgiven.

For what is sin?

**1 John 3:4**
*Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.*

But we who believe not only are forgiven of sins past, but God will not impute sin to us. Our transgression is forgiven. This is a promise of God.

**Hebrews 10:17**
*And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.*

teachings.title: The work of the Holy Ghost
teachings.summary: The Holy Ghost quickens, indwells, comforts and seals believers unto redemption, bears witness that they are God's children, reproves the world, teaches the word and makes intercession.
teachings.text:
The Spirit of God, the Holy Ghost, which was foretold by the prophets who were moved by Him to receive the word of God, inspired, and promised of Christ Jesus to us, the Comforter. That He may dwell within us, the Father and the Son, in the Spirit. Who quickens our dead spirit, our stoney heart, and makes us live again. Who comforts us in tribulations. Who seals us as His own, the earnest of our inheritance in Christ;

**Ephesians 4:30**
*And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption.*

**Ephesians 1:13-14**
*In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.*

This is the promise, that we who are saved may know we are His, and that we know we have eternal life, adopted as joint-heirs, made sons of God;

**Romans 8:16**
*The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God*.

We who the Spirit indwells are given the power to free those we share the truth with from their sins, to be born again of the Spirit as we were. Through the Gospel, which is given by the Spirit of Truth, that by hearing the inspired word of God, they may believe, and by faith be saved, that they may save others in His name, by that same Spirit. Or, if they have not the Spirit of truth, to be condemned, opposing themselves. Anathema.

All men are called by the Spirit, God the Father having lifted up the Son, because the Spirit of the Comforter works to reproved the world of sin, righteousness and judgment. That they may know they need salvation, and believe.

And all knowledge is given by the Holy Ghost, who teaches us all things, making God's word understandable, as we hear His voice and follow Him. And bringing all things to remembrance, that we may be able to give a ready answer for the hope we have in Him.

And by making our prayers effectual, even as we in our sin don't know what we need, the Spirit makes intercession for us before God in Christ's name.

teachings.title: Secret sin and the Father's rod
teachings.summary: God chastens His adopted children and brings secret sins to light, and the guilt of conscience should drive the believer to confess and forsake sin.
teachings.text:
Of course, David takes Bathsheba as his wife, one of many. He lives with his sin and the poor decisions he has made. But the Lord is displeased and David's actions won't remain hidden for long.

**Hebrews 12:6-7**
*For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?*

**Hebrews 10:26-27**
*For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.*

That fearful looking for judgment, the guilt we feel when we disobey God's word, the pangs of our conscience, is a powerful motivation to get right with the Lord. To call out to Christ our redeemer for forgiveness, to repent of our actions and seek to do the right thing. Especially knowing that, as adopted children, our Father will not spare the rod, and the sins we do in secret will be revealed in the light.

**Psalms 90:8**
*Thou hast set our iniquities before thee, our secret sins in the light of thy countenance.*

**Proverbs 28:13**
*He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy*.

**Luke 8:17**
*For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.*

teachings.title: Remaining in the congregation of the dead
teachings.summary: Those who see the way of truth but reject it without truly believing are given over by God to a reprobate mind and cannot be brought again to repentance.
teachings.text:
*The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.*

**1 John 2:19**
*They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.*

**Hebrews 6:4-8** 
*For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame. For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.*

**John 6:64-65**
*But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who should betray him.*

**Proverbs 21:16** is another proof text for the understanding of the reprobate doctrine. The knowledge that a man who wandered out of the way of understanding remains in the congregation of the dead.

Notice it isn't that the person HAS understanding. They are not perfect in their ways. They saw the path, maybe followed it for a while, and left it. They tasted of the Spirit, but rejected it without ingesting, without being indwelled. They never fully believe. And when they reject the truth of God? God gives them up and gives them over. It is impossible for them to come to the knowledge of the truth. To be brought again to repentance.

**Romans 1:21-22**
*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools*

These people knew the truth, but did not glorify Him. They knew the gift, but weren't thankful for it. Their foolish heart was darkened. Hardened. They were waxed fat, dull of hearing. Eyes that could not see.

*Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts...Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections...And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient*.

They are given over to Satan. Reprobate concerning the faith. Clouds without water, twice-dead, branches cut off for unfruitfulness, cast into the fire. Conscience seared.

They remain in the congregation of the dead.

teachings.title: Thou art all fair, my love
teachings.summary: The bride seen without blemish pictures believers made righteous and unblameable in Christ, and the sealed garden pictures eternal security.
teachings.text:
Chapter 4 opens with an ode to the beloved bride by her lover, the bridegroom. When he looks upon her he sees her fair beauty, her eyes as doves', her hair as the flocks of wild mountain goats. Picturing her black, flowing locks as the long, black, silky hair the goats have. When a herd of these dark goats grazes and moves down a steep mountain from a distance, the flowing movement creates a visual illusion of cascading hair.

He compares her teeth to the whitest of sheep, shorn and clean and notes there are none missing, a rarity to be sure in the ancient world.

Her lips, red as scarlet thread and her speech comely. Her temples and neck and breasts and scent, perfect and without blemish.

*Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.*

The poetic nature of the song, romanticizing the couples love, could be seen as hyperbole. The aura of beauty that comes with infatuation. The perfection we see when we are caught up in our love for the other.

But, as a spiritual allegory, we see the woman, who works the field and vineyard, black skinned, is without blemish when the King looks upon her. Just as we who are saved and sanctified by faith in Christ are pure when the Lord looks upon us. Clothed in righteousness. No sin imputed upon our new man.

**2 Corinthians 5:21**
*For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.*

He has made us without blemish;

**Colossians 1:21–22**
*And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight*

Solomon's King sings passionately about his beloved; *How fair is thy love, my sister, my spouse!* A sister of Israel, his spouse through their betrothal and marriage.

This is also how Jesus sees us, His beloved. We are His brothers and sisters, and spouse as a collective. Made one within the body of Christ.

**Matthew 12:50**
*For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother*.

His idealized view of us, despite our sin and despite our falling short of the glory of God, comes entirely by His love for us. That while we were sinners, Christ died for us. That He justifies the ungodly. That the Spirit quickens and seals us unto redemption.

So when Solomon compares his love to an inclosed garden, walled off, a spring shut up, barred from use by others. A fountain sealed, carrying the seal of the King, and so kept pure from pollution. In this allegory we see the promise of eternal security in Christ. We are eternally His.

The fruits of the garden are orchards, even pomegranates, and pleasant fruits, and flowers and spices used in ointments and perfume. Spikenard, the precious Himalayan plant, used to anoint Christ;

**Mark 14:3**
*And being in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster box of ointment of spikenard very precious; and she brake the box, and poured it on his head.*

The odors of her garden are pleasing. Precious to the King.  Just as our fruit, our good works in Christ, are pleasing to Him.

*A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon*. He views us and the works we do for Him the same way, and we issue forth the living waters of the Spirit when we walk in His ways.

The chapter ends shifting to the beloved woman, the bride, calling upon her lord to enter her garden, *that the spices thereof may flow out.* Spiritually, calling upon the name of the Lord, that one may be saved, that God may eat His pleasant fruits.
